Walker won the Junior race followed home by Len Bishop and with our other men packing well, we managed to beat the home team once again. Southgate very kindly provided our lads with tea and cakes after the run and we hope to entertain them over our own course next season.

In the match events, Benstead was 2nd in the 100, while Bishop and Maclean were first home in the 880 yds. Alan Sexton won the 220 yds. and Basil Walden won the 440, while Bob Belmore and Steve Charlton were 2nd and 3rd in the 1 mile match.

The going did not suit Colin Collis at all and Burr and Bishop had obviously not fully recovered from colds. Jim Masters unfortunately injured his foot again on the iron hard ground; he had already done so once this season in the Inter Counties.
Len Bishop ran last and seemed determined that those behind him should remain so and he put up the fastest time of the day with a time only Brown has beaten for us.
A special word of praise for Alan Bishop. From a mediocre half miler (he won't mind me saying that) to 29th in the Poly Marathon in such a short space of time is no mean feat.
On 24th September three of our distance runners, W. Wortley, A, Bishop and J. McDonald, just sufficient for a team, set off on the long run to Brighton.
On turning into Cambridge Road, Dave Baulch and Pete Bagnall pulled away slightly from Charlie Walker and these three were then some forty yards ahead of Davidson, Flanagan and Bishop.
Bishop 19th, which gave us 2nd team place behind Southend.
